Recruit Holdings profit jumps as Indeed monetisation boosts first-half earnings
sum: Investing.com -- Recruit Holdings reported a sharp increase in first-half profit, supported by stronger revenue and improved monetisation at its Indeed job-search platform, particularly in the United States, where hiring demand remained stagnant.

Profit attributable for the six months ended September 30 rose 65.7% to ¥411.6 billion, while revenue increased 19.3% to ¥2.14 trillion. Operating income climbed 63.9% to ¥513.7 billion, and EBITDA+S rose 49.7% to ¥590.8 billion.

The HR Technology business was the biggest growth driver, with revenue increasing 35.6% to ¥945.5 billion. U.S. revenue rose 45.5% to ¥551.8 billion in yen terms, as monetisation improvements lifted average revenue per job posting on Indeed by 37% year over year, despite stagnant hiring demand.

Revenue at the Staffing business increased 10.6% to ¥917.5 billion, while Marketing Matching Technologies revenue grew 3.6% to ¥291.4 billion, supported by stronger demand in its Lifestyle business, including Beauty.

Recruit maintained its full-year revenue forecast of ¥4.23 trillion and operating income target of ¥945 billion, alongside its net profit outlook of ¥755 billion. It said HR Technology was expected to exceed its previous full-year outlook, but the impact on consolidated guidance remained limited.
The company raised its interim dividend to ¥13 per share from ¥12.50 a year earlier and maintained its full-year dividend forecast at ¥26 per share.
It is also continuing a share buyback programme of up to ¥350 billion, covering a maximum of 64 million shares, through March 31, 2027.

Hussey, known as "Mr Cricket" for his technical expertise, will also provide coaching assistance during this month's home T20 series against England and the subsequent four-Test series against New Zealand.
He will additionally work with Australia during the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, where cricket is on the agenda, and the T20 World Cup in 2028.

TCS Shares Rise 4% As Q2 Profit Beats Estimates, AI Revenue Crosses $3.1 Bn
sum: Annualised revenue from AI services crosses USD 3.1 billion, taking the business beyond 10 per cent of its overall revenue run rate

Shares of Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) rose more than 2 per cent in early trade on Friday, as investors focused on stronger-than-expected September-quarter profit and growing artificial intelligence (AI) revenue, setting aside near-term concerns over the US suspension of the company from its employment-based green card programme.

The stock opened 0.48 per cent higher at Rs 2,086 apiece on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) before climbing 2.12 per cent to Rs 2,120.10. The positive reaction followed TCS reporting a 4 per cent sequential increase in net profit to Rs 13,884 crore for the second quarter, ahead of analyst estimates tracked by Bloomberg.

Revenue rose 1.3 per cent quarter-on-quarter to Rs 73,188 crore, broadly in line with expectations. Earnings before interest and tax increased 1.4 per cent to Rs 17,553 crore, while the operating margin edged up to 24 per cent from 23.95 per cent in the June quarter.

Investor attention also centred on TCS’ expanding AI business and a series of strategic partnerships announced during the quarter. The company said annualised revenue from AI services had crossed USD 3.1 billion, taking the business beyond 10 per cent of its overall revenue run rate.

Among its key announcements was a five-year strategic partnership with Porsche AG, under which TCS will acquire the entire stake in MHP, the German automaker’s management and IT consulting subsidiary. TCS also agreed to take over Best Buy’s Global Capability Centre in India and convert it into a dedicated AI Capability Centre focused on developing advanced AI-powered solutions.

TCS Chief Executive Officer and Managing Director K Krithivasan described the Porsche and Best Buy agreements as a new category of transformation partnerships, aimed at building platforms that can deliver AI-driven value at scale.

sum: The Nikkei stock benchmark gained after a three-day holiday as Tokyo’s market caught up with a global AI-led rally. Climbing bond yields and a rise in oil prices weighed on broader risk appetite, however.

The Nikkei 225 rose 1.8% to 66,167.25 as of 10:09 a.m. in Tokyo, while the broader Topix rose 0.2% to 4,097.42. Chip-related firms like Ibiden Co. and Socionext Inc. were among the Nikkei’s best performers, while software names like Baycurrent Inc. and Recruit Holdings Co. weighed. The Topix was led by electronics and machinery makers, with banks and services weak.

While Japan was closed for its Silver Week holiday, the global AI trade gathered steam thanks to early signs of success for Meta Platforms Inc.’s new AI agent and Alibaba Group Holding Ltd.’s unveiling of what it calls China’s most powerful AI chip. The Nasdaq 100 hit a fresh record high on Tuesday, although US equities pared gains on Wednesday amid inflation concerns.
“We expect the semiconductor-heavy Nikkei 225 to take cues from the strength in global technology stocks,” said Hu You, a senior research analyst at iFast Financial in Singapore.

Japan’s broad range of chip material makers makes it well positioned to benefit from renewed bullishness around AI, said You. Ibiden is a particular winner as the chip package substrate maker is set to gain from the increasing complexity of AI semiconductors and demand for advanced packaging, she added.
But volatility in the yen, which is trading around 158 to the dollar, is likely to keep investors cautious, You said.
Climbing global bond yields are another concern. Japan’s benchmark 10-year government bond yield rose eight basis points to 3.055% on Thursday morning, tracking moves in the Treasury market.

Nikkei extends gains, briefly tops 65,800 as U.S. semiconductor rally over holiday weekend provides tailwind
sum: The Nikkei Stock Average opened higher on the Tokyo Stock Exchange on September 24, extending its winning streak. The opening level was 65,476.44, up 457.49 points from the September 18 close before the Silver Week holiday. After the open, gains widened to more than 600 points, and the index briefly surged over 800 points to the 65,800 level in early trading. The buying momentum that swept through AI and semiconductor stocks in U.S. markets during the holiday carried over into related names on the Tokyo exchange.

Among semiconductor-related stocks, Advantest, Tokyo Electron, and Ibiden opened sharply higher. SoftBank Group, whose U.K.-based chip design subsidiary Arm Holdings posted significant gains during the holiday, briefly surged more than 7%. Fast Retailing, a heavyweight contributor to the index, also traded firmly. On the downside, Toyota Motor and Sony Group edged lower, while Recruit Holdings, Mitsubishi Corp., and banking stocks including Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group declined. The Tokyo Stock Price Index (TOPIX) rebounded.

During the holiday period, the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite hit a three-and-a-half-month high on September 21 in U.S. markets. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index (SOX), which tracks major semiconductor-related names, climbed roughly 8% from September 18 through September 23. In Japan, buying was concentrated in high-priced semiconductor stocks that carry significant weight in the Nikkei average.

The decline in crude oil prices also supported investor sentiment. NYMEX crude oil futures settled in the $92-per-barrel range on September 23. Prices had hovered around $100 before Japan's holiday, but excessive concerns over Middle East supply disruptions eased, bringing prices lower. The fading risk of corporate earnings deterioration and inflation concerns stemming from high oil prices has reinforced the bullish stance.

Developments surrounding U.S.-China trade negotiations also provided a tailwind for the market. Ahead of the U.S.-China summit on September 24, U.S. Treasury Secretary Bessent reportedly said on September 23 that the two sides had agreed to extend the trade war ceasefire—set to expire on November 10—by two months.

Michigan NFL Draft Stock Watch: Bryce Underwood Tumbles Down Boards
sum: Bryce Underwood came to Ann Arbor for $15 million. And from the jump, nothing less than an eventual bona fide superstar under center has been expected by Michigan faithful and analysts alike. It was simply impossible to project Underwood through collegiate coaching with the frame, speed, arm strength, and work ethic he possesses without arriving at a glowing prognosis for how his career will develop.
Entering college as the number one overall recruit and with everything seemingly working in his favor, Underwood had been a long presumed early selection of the 2028 NFL Draft. Why wouldn’t he be?
Well, his performance against Western Michigan provides a couple clues.

It’s important to preface this section with the note that single collegiate performances rarely overhaul a given prospect’s professional outlook, especially for athletes still years removed from entering the draft. Yes, NFL franchises evaluate talents based on in-game performances, but they also place as much, if not more, emphasis on measurables and future potential when examining a player. Normally, 48 minute snippets of a player’s resume won’t completely change the calculus.

Yet that’s exactly what Bryce Underwood’s season opening performance has done. His dud against Western Michigan did not change how tall he is, how agile he is, or how hard he throws a football. What it did do is raise the question of whether he can improve.

That’s the real issue with the Western Michigan game. Underwood had had an offseason of presumably the first fully competent coaching he’s received in college to make necessary strides from an up and down freshman campaign. Yet such strides were not taken. Rather, Underwood looked skittish in the pocket, stared down receivers, and time after time made the incorrect throw against basic coverages. Regression, not improvement, was the story of the day.

items.t: Xingyu Automotive Lighting's H1 net profit falls 5% but still pays 56.64 million yuan dividend; fallout from graduate-recruit layoff controversy lingers
sum: On the evening of August 26, Xingyu Automotive Lighting Systems (601799.SS) disclosed its 2026 interim report. During the reporting period, the company achieved revenue of 6.884 billion yuan (approximately $1.0 billion), up 1.87% year-on-year; net profit attributable to shareholders of the listed company was 669 million yuan (approximately $99.7 million), down 5.26% year-on-year. Despite earnings pressure, the company still plans to distribute a cash dividend of 2.00 yuan per 10 shares to all shareholders, totaling approximately 56.64 million yuan (approximately $8.4 million). The proposal was approved unanimously by the board with 7 votes.

Less than a month before this earnings release, this leading Chinese automotive lighting company had just weathered a public relations storm that swept across the internet. In early August, Xingyu Automotive Lighting Systems, citing "business difficulties" and "poor market conditions," summoned 2026 fresh graduates who had been on the job for only one month for group interviews, offering them two options: "voluntary resignation" or "reassignment to frontline operator positions." Ultimately, 107 people had their labor contracts terminated. After an investigation, the Changzhou Municipal Human Resources and Social Security Bureau reported that the company's negotiation process was "crude and rigid, lacking sufficient and effective communication," and suspended the HR director from duty.

Judging from the interim report data, Xingyu Automotive Lighting Systems faced a classic "revenue growth without profit growth" dilemma in the first half. On the revenue side, the company undertook R&D projects for 59 vehicle models' lighting systems and achieved mass production for 46 models during the period, both increases from the same period last year, driving modest revenue growth. On the profit side, however, the company was squeezed by weak domestic passenger vehicle sales, underperforming volumes for certain supported models, and rising raw material prices, resulting in a 5.26% year-on-year decline in net profit attributable to shareholders.
Changes in the expense structure further confirm the source of operating pressure.

sum: Shares of Recruit Holdings (6098.T), a major Japanese staffing and human resources services company, hit their daily limit up on August 10. The surge came after the company's first-quarter (April-June) results for the fiscal year ending March 2026, released the previous weekend, significantly beat market expectations, and a major European brokerage raised its target price by 33.6% to ¥17,100, triggering concentrated buying from investors.

The company's first-quarter operating profit expanded sharply, rising 66.1% year-on-year to ¥255.4 billion (approximately $1.6 billion). Market expectations had been for just under ¥200 billion (approximately $1.3 billion), making the magnitude of the upside surprise particularly impactful for investors. The full-year operating profit forecast was also revised upward, from the previous ¥787 billion (approximately $5.0 billion) to ¥945 billion (approximately $6.0 billion), representing a 49.9% increase from the prior fiscal year. This new guidance far exceeds the market consensus, which was seen at just over ¥800 billion (approximately $5.1 billion).

The HR Technology segment was the primary driver of the strong results. While the total number of job listings on the job search engine Indeed remained sluggish, the paid job advertising service "Premium Sponsored Jobs" gained strong momentum, particularly in the U.S. market, contributing significantly to revenue growth.

In response to the robust earnings, a major European brokerage reaffirmed its "Buy" rating on Recruit Holdings on August 7, while raising its target price from ¥12,800 to ¥17,100. Based on the consensus rating of 4.93 from 14 analysts as of August 6, which already reflected a bullish stance, and a consensus target price of ¥13,286, the new target represents a bullish assessment that exceeds the market average by more than 28%.

The stock reacted to this double dose of positive news, with buying pushing the price up to the daily limit. The market has once again recognized the earnings power of the HR Technology segment, and expectations for further full-year earnings upside are also rising.

Between 2019–20 and 2024–25, the share of uncertified teachers (i.e., teachers without any state certification) more than tripled. Despite this statewide surge, district-level certification rates varied considerably across contexts, with some districts maintaining high teacher certification rates. Interviewed leaders—from districts selected for having high certification rates and/or noted success in supporting the certification process—highlighted key strategies to prioritize certification: (1) preparation partnerships to increase the pipeline of new certified teachers, (2) prioritization of certification in recruitment and hiring practices, (3) salary incentives along with tracking and dedicated staff to support uncertified teachers toward certification, and (4) retention of new teachers through mentoring and specific supports. House Bill 2, landmark legislation passed by the Texas legislature in 2025, offers districts unprecedented financial investments in recruitment, preparation, certification, and mentoring that can increase the rate of certified teachers.

Texas employs the largest teacher workforce of all states in the United States, and the state consistently posts teacher attrition rates higher than the national average. Texas schools have had to hire more than 40,000 teachers per year to replace those exiting the profession. In the 2022–23 through 2024–25 school years, more than two thirds of these newly hired teachers entered the profession either on emergency permits, while completing preparation (i.e., interns), or without any state certification (i.e., uncertified). While teachers entering through such pathways can fill classroom vacancies quickly, Texas-based research has found that they are less likely to stay in the profession and tend to be less effective than other new teachers.Kirksey, J. sum: It’s an executive’s nightmare: A product violates privacy laws, drawing regulators’ ire and igniting a media scandal. And when AI contributes to the mistake, the public’s trust can be even harder for the company to restore.

That’s what happened to Kentaro Mori, who led risk management in 2019 at Recruit Holdings, the Japanese human resources technology company that owns popular job-search sites Indeed and Glassdoor. He woke up on his birthday expecting well wishes and instead found his cell phone ringing about a subsidiary that was accused of running students’ data through an algorithm—without their consent—to predict whether they would accept jobs, then sharing those predictions with hiring companies.

Early in AI’s adoption, the lapse in judgment hit a nerve. Students were outraged, Japan’s privacy commission admonished the company, and the public cried foul, saying Recruit’s algorithm unfairly excluded candidates from being considered for positions.
“You can offend the public deeply by using AI in a way they don't approve of,” explains Harvard Business School Professor Sandra Sucher. “A good answer will never be, ‘AI made me do it.’”

Sucher studies how companies can build trust, including through responsible AI use, and finds a ready roadmap in the way Recruit acknowledged its mistake, apologized, and ultimately recovered from the misstep. She chronicles the company’s journey through an HBS case study and supplement, “Recruit Holdings Co. Ltd.: Managing Innovation and Trust in the Age of AI” and B, which raise important questions as companies move to incorporate AI into their operations.

“What kinds of decisions are people comfortable having an algorithm make on behalf of the firm? And what kinds of decisions should firms be making themselves in order to be held accountable for their actions?” asks Sucher, the MBA Class of 1966 Professor of Management Practice. “These are forever questions, but AI has amplified them because of the number of decisions that it can help with, and the current rush to adopt it. Companies appear to be turning over responsibility for decisions that they nonetheless are still on the hook for.”
Sucher outlines six key questions executives should ask to make sure their companies’ use of AI earns—and maintains—public trust.

sum: NASSAU, Bahamas — Drill sergeants assigned to the Recruiting and Retention Battalion, Rhode Island Army National Guard (RIARNG), conducted a five-day subject matter expert exchange (SMEE) with Royal Bahamas Defence Force (RBDF) Ranger instructors, to share best practices in training, leadership, and recruit development from March 9 – 13, 2026, at Coral Harbour, The Bahamas. The SMEE provided an exchange of shared objectives while strengthening trust and interoperability between U.S. and Bahamian forces.

“Their Ranger program is very comparable to our JROTC (Junior Reserve Officers’ Training Corps) and our RSP (Recruit Sustainment Program),” said Staff Sgt. William Naylor, drill sergeant, RIARNG. “We discussed how we conducted certain things within our program, to see how we could help streamline or enhance the RBDF Ranger program.”
The RBDF Ranger program is a structured youth development program that prepares young Bahamians for potential military service by emphasizing discipline, leadership, and basic military skills.

Naylor and fellow drill sergeants, Sgt. 1st Class Angel Mercado and Sgt. Bevin Pryce, opened the SMEE by outlining the RSP phases—red, white, blue, green and gold—that prepare U.S. Army recruits for basic combat training (BCT). “In red phase, we talk about breaking the Soldier down from an individual and turning them into a more team-oriented individual,” said Pryce. “We discussed a little bit of everything from each phase, how we break them down and we build them back up; what a training cycle looks like.”

Throughout the engagement, participants discussed instructional strategies such as structured teaching methods, risk mitigation and how to effectively manage training environments for students of varying experience levels. Drill sergeants shared techniques such as the Army’s “crawl, walk, run” method, breaking down complex tasks into manageable steps while reinforcing core values and leadership principles.
Leading Woman Marine Yazmine Pickering, a Ranger instructor, said one of the most impactful lessons was the emphasis on standardized instruction and structure.

items.t: Germany turns to Indian workers to help solve labour shortage
sum: Germany has a shortage of workers - so it's turning to India for help

Germany is continuing to struggle with a shortage of skilled workers, as elderly staff retire, and there are not enough young candidates to fill their roles. To try to alleviate the problem the country is increasingly turning to workers from India.
For Handirk von Ungern-Sternberg, it started with an email that dropped into his inbox in February 2021. It had come from India.
The gist of the message was: "We have lots of young, motivated people looking for vocational training and we're wondering if you're interested."

Von Ungern-Sternberg was working for the Freiburg Chamber of Skilled Crafts in southwest Germany, a trade body that represents skilled workers, from bricklayers and carpenters, to butchers and bakers, and the companies that employ them.
"We had a lot of desperate employers, who couldn't find anyone to work for them," says Von Ungern-Sternberg. "So we decided to give it a chance."
His first call was to the head of the local butchers' guild. Butchers all over Germany were having a particularly hard time. It was a sector in marked decline.

With Jam Miller moving on, Alabama's running back depth chart is wide open and Crowell is built to take advantage. The 5-foot-11, 210-pounder brings a physical, downhill running style and a proven track record of production after reclassifying from the 2027 class. He rushed for 2,632 yards and 35 touchdowns in his final season, earning Alabama Mr. Football and Gatorade Player of the Year honors. China in ‘covert and calculated’ effort to recruit MPs and peers, minister says | Espionage
sum: MPs and peers have been told they face “a covert and calculated” attempt to recruit parliamentarians through two LinkedIn profiles linked to the Chinese intelligence service.

After MI5 issued an espionage alert on Tuesday, saying that two people were operating on LinkedIn to obtain “non-public and insider insights”, the security minister, Dan Jarvis, told MPs the effort was focused on those “with access to sensitive information about parliament and the UK government”.

With the Chinese embassy in London dismissing the accusations as “pure fabrication”, the diplomatic dispute appeared to be a new flashpoint in the increasingly tense relationship between China and the UK over alleged espionage.

MI5 said the profiles were under the names Amanda Qiu, from BP-YR Executive Search, and Shirly Shen, who is linked to InternshipUnion, and told MPs and peers they were using LinkedIn to “conduct outreach at scale”.

The spy agency sent its warning to the speaker of the Commons, Lindsay Hoyle, and his Lords equivalent, John McFall, on Tuesday morning, both of whom relayed its contents to the members of their houses with a cover message.

In his email to peers, McFall said the individuals, linked to China’s ministry of state security spy agency (MSS), were aiming “to collect information and lay the groundwork for long-term relationships, using professional networking sites, recruitment agents and consultants acting on their behalf”.

Qiu’s profile on LinkedIn, written in English, describes her as having been the chief executive of BP-YR Executive Search for more than six years and says she is based in Beijing. Her listed interests include the UK’s Department for Transport and the Tony Blair Institute.

sum: As Iowa women's basketball continues to bring in several talented prospects to Iowa City, the Hawkeyes welcomed 2027 four-star power forward recruit Destiny Manyawu, who shared photos from the unofficial visit she took to Iowa City earlier this week.

The 6-foot-3 power forward from Kansas City, Missouri, is the younger sister of Iowa men's basketball junior forward Cam Manyawu, and ranks as the No. 25 overall recruit, No. 7 power forward, and No. 1 prospect in the state, according to Rivals.
Manyawu currently stars for Staley High School in Kansas City, and also plays club for the Mokan Girls Basketball program on the Nike EYBL circuit.
Iowa extended an offer to Manyawu on June 12, which adds to her plethora of scholarship invitations from programs nationwide.
Among the bevy of teams offering scholarships to the skilled Missourian, in addition to Iowa, are fellow Big Ten foes Nebraska, Wisconsin, Minnesota, Illinois, Oregon, Ohio State, and Michigan.

Although the familial connection gives the Hawkeyes a slight advantage in the early stages of Manyawu's recruitment, Iowa will certainly have its work cut out against a bevy of other elite programs also vying for her future commitment.
